extracted.intended_audience: members of the public (including potential commenters), political committees and their counsel, and other stakeholders interested in FEC rulemaking on electronic contributions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for submitting public comments to the Federal Election Commission on a petition for rulemaking about electronic payment methods; also describes the petition's requested regulatory standards for campaign contribution recordkeeping and acceptance. Covers deadlines, required commenter information, public-record notification, and the proposed amendments to 11 CFR 104.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments close date / deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted on or before January 27, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DATES section specifies the deadline; the Commission will not consider the Petition's merits until after the comment period closes.

rubrics_metrics.name: All comments must be in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments must be in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may submit comments electronically via the Commission's website at https://sers.fec.gov/​fosers/​, reference REG 2024-08. (This identifies acceptable submission format and docket reference.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Required commenter identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each commenter must provide, at a minimum, his or her first name, last name, city and state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this minimum information is required for a comment to be properly submitted and made part of the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments and attachments become public record
rubrics_metrics.description: All properly submitted comments, including attachments, will become part of the public record, and the Commission will make comments available for public viewing on the Commission's website and in the Commission's Public Records Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because comments are public, commenters should not include information they do not wish to make public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid including sensitive/personal/private information in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters should not provide in their comments any information that they do not wish to make public, such as a home street address, personal email address, date of birth, phone number, social security number, or driver's license number, or any information that is restricted from disclosure, such as trade secrets or commercial or financial information that is privileged or confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a clear admonition to redact or omit personally identifying or legally protected information from submissions because everything properly submitted becomes publicly viewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to inspect the Petition and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The public may inspect the Petition on the Commission's website at http://www.fec.gov/​fosers/​ (reference REG 2024-08).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments will also be made available on the Commission's website and in the Commission's Public Records Office; use the referenced docket number when searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural timing for Commission consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not consider the Petition's merits until after the comment period closes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commission decides the Petition has merit, it may begin a rulemaking proceeding and will announce any action in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official PDF for legal citation / verification
rubrics_metrics.description: This site is a prototype XML rendition and is not the official legal edition; use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify against an official edition of the Federal Register for legal research; XML on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice until ACFR grants official status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing statutory/regulatory disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Political committees are required to disclose identifying information from each contributor, including name, address, and—in some cases—the contributor's occupation and employer (52 U.S.C. 30104; 11 CFR 104.3, 104.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These existing disclosure rules form the baseline context for the Petition requesting additional verification requirements for electronic payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing contribution limits and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Election Campaign Act limits the total amount a contributor may contribute to any given political committee and prohibits certain persons from making contributions; it also prohibits any person from making a contribution in the name of another person (see cited statutory provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Petition is framed as addressing potential circumvention of these statutory limits and prohibitions via fraudulent electronic payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed recordkeeping requirement (amend 11 CFR 104.14(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 104.14(b)(5) to provide that records for contributions made by credit, debit, prepaid, or gift card must include documentation confirming that a cross-check occurred between the contributor's self-reported identifying information with the card issuing institution's own information on the name and billing address of the cardholder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Petition contends this documentation would help detect straw donor/fraudulent transactions by verifying the contributor's supplied info against issuer records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed acceptance restriction for prepaid/gift cards (amend 11 CFR 104.14(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 104.14(e) to provide that contributions cannot be accepted from prepaid or gift cards unless the information from those prepaid or gift cards can be cross-checked with the card issuing institution to confirm the name and billing address required under paragraph (b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This would effectively prohibit accepting prepaid/gift card contributions unless issuer cross-check is feasible, addressing Petition's concern that prepaid cards are often used in fraudulent transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested security measure: compare contributor info to card-issuer billing data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Petition states that 'specific security measures can mitigate this problem,' such as comparing the identifying information supplied by contributors to the name, address, and other billing information on file with the issuer of the credit card used to make the contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This example is given as an illustrative mitigation technique and is the practical basis for the proposed regulatory cross-check requirement.
